what_its_for: Fostemsavir is an HIV medicine used to treat adults with HIV-1 infection. It is used when other HIV medicines are no longer working well or cannot be tolerated. It works by blocking HIV from entering your body's immune cells, helping to lower the amount of HIV in your blood and keep your immune system stronger.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with or without food. Do NOT crush, chew, or break the tablet. Take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Fostemsavir must always be used together with other HIV medicines — never take it alone.
dosing: The usual dose for adults is 600 mg (one tablet) taken twice daily — once in the morning and once in the evening, about 12 hours apart. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions, as your dose may be different based on other medicines you take.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the tablets in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Protect from moisture. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use past the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking certain medicines that can interact with fostemsavir, including rifampin (an antibiotic), carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital (seizure medicines), enzalutamide (a cancer medicine), and St. John's Wort (an herbal supplement) — these can make fostemsavir stop working. Also avoid starting any new prescription, over-the-counter, or herbal medicines without first checking with your doctor or pharmacist. Fostemsavir does NOT prevent spreading HIV to others, so continue to use safer sex practices.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you notice: yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice), dark urine, unusual tiredness, stomach pain, or signs of liver problems. Also call your doctor if you develop a skin rash, signs of immune reconstitution syndrome (new or worsening infections or inflammation shortly after starting treatment), irregular heartbeat or heart palpitations, dizziness or fainting, or if you feel your HIV medicines are not working. Tell your doctor immediately if you become pregnant while taking this medicine.
when_it_works: Fostemsavir starts working right away in your body, but you may not feel different at first. Most people see their HIV viral load (the amount of HIV in the blood) decrease within a few weeks of starting treatment. It may take several months to reach undetectable levels. It is very important to keep taking all your HIV medicines every day, even when you feel well, to keep the virus under control.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of fostemsavir during pregnancy is not fully known. Breastfeeding is not recommended for people with HIV because HIV can be passed to the baby through breast milk. Liver problems: Use with caution if you have liver disease, including hepatitis B or C co-infection. Your doctor may monitor your liver more closely. Kidney problems: No dose adjustment is generally needed for kidney disease, but tell your doctor about any kidney issues. Children: Fostemsavir is currently approved only for adults. It has not been studied enough in children to be used safely.
